questions.prompt: A binary symmetric channel has crossover probability $\varepsilon=0.2$. Compute its capacity in bits per channel use. (tolerance 0.002)
questions.explanation: **Numeric answer: 0.278** (tolerance 0.002). Capacity is 1 − h₂(0.2) = 1 − 0.722 = 0.278 bits, attained by a uniform input. At ε = 0.5 it would be 0, and at ε = 1 it returns to a full bit, so capacity is not monotone in the crossover probability.

questions.prompt: A binary erasure channel erases each symbol with probability $0.3$. Compute its capacity in bits per channel use. (tolerance 0.002)
questions.explanation: **Numeric answer: 0.7** (tolerance 0.002). Capacity is 1 − 0.3 = 0.7 bits. Compare this with the BSC above: an erasure that announces itself costs far less than a flip of the same probability, because the receiver knows which positions are unreliable.

questions.prompt: Signal power and noise power satisfy $P/N=7$ in an AWGN channel. Compute the capacity in bits per real channel use. (tolerance 0.002)
questions.explanation: **Numeric answer: 1.5** (tolerance 0.002). Capacity is ½ log₂(1 + 7) = ½ · 3 = 1.5 bits. The factor of one half belongs to one real discrete use of the channel; the bandwidth form in bits per second uses a different normalization.

questions.prompt: A Z-channel flips input 1 to output 0 with probability $\alpha=0.25$ and leaves input 0 untouched. The optimal input uses symbol 1 with probability about $0.4278$. Compute the capacity in bits per channel use. (tolerance 0.003)
questions.explanation: **Numeric answer: 0.558** (tolerance 0.003). The capacity is about 0.558 bits. Note that the optimal input is not uniform: the vulnerable symbol is used less than half the time, because the channel treats the two inputs asymmetrically.
